## The course in one paragraph

*From Data to Models with R* is an open, beginner-friendly course in R programming and applied statistics. It starts from the very first line of R code and arrives at regression models, machine learning, dimensionality reduction and clustering, with an optional deep-learning track. It is designed for university students — and anyone else — who need to analyse data but **do not have a rigorous statistical background**: every statistical idea is introduced through a concrete problem, a picture or a simulation before any formula. The material can support a university module of up to **9 ECTS (about 72 contact hours)** and is freely available on GitHub.

## Prerequisites

- **No previous programming experience** is required.
- **No previous statistics course** is required: Levels 2 and 3 build descriptive statistics, probability and inference from scratch. Students who already know these topics can move faster through them.
- Basic computer literacy (managing files and folders, installing software) and a laptop on which you can install R and an editor. Many exercises also run in the browser, with nothing to install.
- For the optional deep-learning lessons: a working local installation of `keras3` (see [Lesson 61](lessons/13-deep-learning/61-dl-setup.qmd)).

## Learning outcomes

**Knowledge.** By the end of the course students will understand:

- the role of R as an environment for data analysis, visualisation and reproducible reporting, and its main object types;
- the basic ideas of descriptive statistics, probability, sampling variability and statistical inference, including the correct interpretation of confidence intervals and p-values;
- the logic of statistical models (linear and generalised linear models) and of supervised and unsupervised learning, including how models are validated and why they can overfit;
- (optional track) the building blocks of neural networks and how they relate to statistical models.

**Skills.** Students will be able to:

- organise an analysis as a reproducible R project and write clear, modern R code (tidyverse, functions, iteration);
- import, clean, reshape and join real data, and handle missing values in a principled way;
- describe data with tables, summary statistics and well-designed ggplot2 graphics;
- choose, run and interpret common tests and confidence intervals, and report effect sizes;
- fit, diagnose, compare and interpret regression models and machine-learning models with tidymodels;
- apply PCA, factor analysis, correspondence analysis and clustering methods, and critically assess their results.

**Communication.** Students will be able to explain methods, assumptions, results and limitations in plain language, in written reports generated directly from code with Quarto.

## Suggested schedule (72 hours)

The schedule is indicative; instructors can adapt it.

| Hours | Modules | Topics |
|:---:|---|---|
| 12 | 1–2 | R, editors and projects; data types, vectors, factors, lists; data frames and dplyr; joins and reshaping |
| 6 | 3–4 | Functions, conditionals, loops and iteration; importing/exporting data; missing data |
| 8 | 5–6 | Frequency tables, summary statistics, two-variable descriptions; ggplot2; correlation |
| 12 | 7–8 | Probability by simulation; distributions; sampling distributions; bootstrap; confidence intervals; hypothesis tests; t-tests, χ² tests, non-parametric tests, ANOVA |
| 14 | 9–10 | Linear, logistic and Poisson regression; model selection; penalised regression; the ML workflow with tidymodels; trees, random forests, boosting, SVMs |
| 10 | 11–12 | PCA, factor analysis, correspondence analysis, MDS, t-SNE/UMAP; k-means, hierarchical, DBSCAN, model-based and spectral clustering |
| 10 | Capstone | Guided end-to-end project and presentations |
| *optional 6–10* | 13 | Deep learning with keras3: dense networks, autoencoders, LSTM/GRU, CNNs |

## How the material is built

- Every lesson is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org) document: text, code and results come from the same source, so the output you see is the output the code produces.
- Interactive exercises run in your browser with [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/) through the [quarto-live](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/) extension.
- Machine learning uses the [tidymodels](https://www.tidymodels.org) framework; [Lesson 44](lessons/10-ml/44-ml-workflow.qmd) explains why it replaced `caret` in this course.
- Figures use a colour-blind-friendly palette.

## Recommended free resources

- Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel & Grolemund, *R for Data Science* (2e) — <https://r4ds.hadley.nz>
- Çetinkaya-Rundel & Hardin, *Introduction to Modern Statistics* (2e) — <https://openintro-ims.netlify.app>
- James, Witten, Hastie & Tibshirani, *An Introduction to Statistical Learning* (2e) — <https://www.statlearning.com>
- Kuhn & Silge, *Tidy Modeling with R* — <https://www.tmwr.org>
- Venables, Smith & R Core Team, *An Introduction to R* — on CRAN
